tips.title: Choosing the Right Cement for ABS vs Polystyrene
tips.text: Tamiya Extra Thin Cement bonds polystyrene perfectly by melting the plastic together, but it struggles with ABS parts found in many modern kits (breeches, gun barrels, ICM and Arma Hobby aircraft propellers). For ABS, switch to Tamiya ABS & Polystyrene Cement in the green bottle, which contains ABS-compatible solvents. Apply sparingly with a fine brush to both surfaces, press together for 10 seconds, and let cure for 24 hours before sanding. Test the bond on a spare sprue first.

tips.title: Selecting Paint Type for Model Kits
tips.text: For most model kits, Vallejo Acrylic Paints offer excellent adhesion and color choice. They're water-based, non-toxic, and easy to clean. However, for historical accuracy or special effects, consider enamels like AMMO by Mig Jimenez. For lacquers, use Alclad II for metal finishes, applying with an HVLP spray gun at 20-30 psi. Acrylics are generally best for detail work and weathering, while enamels and lacquers are better for large, flat surfaces.

tips.title: Choosing the Right Sandpaper Grits
tips.text: For sanding plastic model parts, start with 220 grit for initial smoothing, followed by 320 grit for fine sanding. For resin parts, use 150 grit initially, then 220 grit. Always sand in one direction, then change the direction for the next grit. Wet sanding with water or soap solution reduces dust and improves cutting. After sanding, wipe parts with a damp cloth and let dry before painting.

tips.title: Selecting Filler for Model Kit Gaps
tips.text: For small gaps, use Vallejo Plastic Putty, applied with a spatula, smoothed with a brush, and let dry before sanding. For larger gaps or deep recesses, mix Tamiya Extra Thin Cement with baking soda until it forms a thick paste. Apply with a toothpick, let dry, sand smooth. For complex shapes, use clear silicone putty from Clear Prop Models, applied thinly, let dry, and sand smooth.

tips.title: Choosing Decal Setting Solutions
tips.text: For most decals, use Microscale Micro Set and Micro Sol to improve adhesion and reduce silvering. Apply Micro Set to the decal and the model surface, let sit for 10 seconds, then apply Micro Sol to the decal only. Let sit until the decal wrinkles, then use a soft brush to slide the decal into place. Let dry completely before handling. For self-adhesive waterslide decals, use Mr. Mark Softer to help slide the decal into position.
